nodes.label: Three Storage Classes, Three Lifecycles
nodes.rationale: Source (never re-derivable, cold), derivative (deterministically re-derivable, warm), preview (cheap, hot). Treating them the same is the most common way this kind of app becomes slow and fat.

nodes.label: Sources Are Path-Addressed, Not Content-Addressed
nodes.rationale: One directory per model named after the part, mirroring the ingest tree, with metadata.json beside the file — the owner wants a folder a user can open in a file manager and find their model by name, not by hash. The cost stated plainly: source deduplication is gone, and it is not recoverable by cleverness, because a store cannot be both one file per model and one file per distinct content.

nodes.label: Content Addressing Survives For blobs/ Only
nodes.rationale: Derivatives only — evictable and rebuildable, never the source of truth. Two-level hex sharding gives 65,536 buckets, keeping any cache directory under ~2k entries at a million derivatives, keyed on BLAKE3.

nodes.label: The blobs/ Naming Gap
nodes.rationale: The design called the cache cache/blobs/ and hung a product rule on the name: 'eviction must never read as data loss' is self-evident to anyone opening a directory called cache/. What shipped is blobs/ as a sibling of libraries/ — never-deleted user data and a freely evictable cache side by side, with nothing on disk saying which is which. Recorded rather than argued away; the distinction lives only in UI wording until blob_path changes.

nodes.label: folder.slug Is The Address, folder.name Is The Label
nodes.rationale: Decided 2026-09-07: a rename is a correction to a label, and rewriting every file under WIP because somebody renamed it Archive 2024 is not what that person asked for. If the slug followed the name, slug_path would answer the new directory and the next ingest into that same category would land there — one category, two directories, and another with every rename. PgFolders::rename cannot write a slug; only reslug repoints a category. Scans match by slug, so a renamed library is found rather than forked.

nodes.label: Upgrading A Store Created Before This Layout
nodes.rationale: The store moved out of the lapidary-blobs named volume into a bind-mounted host directory and nothing copies it across. Skip the copy and nothing fails at boot — the grid still renders because thumbnails are bytea in Postgres — so the first symptom is a download answering 500, and migrate_storage loops on ENOENT. Nothing is deleted, so it is recoverable after the fact as well as before.

nodes.label: Per-Role Compression With Trained Zstd Dictionaries
nodes.rationale: A pure age rule compresses the derivatives on the hot open path for ~2% space and an added decode stage, so role comes first and age second. A library is hundreds of structurally similar STEP files sharing headers and unit definitions: train per library for 20-40% better ratio. Dictionaries are immutable content-addressed artifacts — losing or mutating one makes blobs unreadable.

nodes.label: Nightly Tiering Job
nodes.rationale: Recompresses cold source blobs from -3 to -19, only when idle over 10 minutes, idempotent, resumable, abortable, rate-limited to one core. The atomic rename is the commit point, so a read arriving mid-recompression gets the old blob and nothing ever blocks a read.

nodes.label: Batched Access Tracking
nodes.rationale: An UPDATE per read turns a read-mostly workload into a write-heavy one and leaves a dead tuple per read — a grid scroll touching 300 thumbnails would be 300 writes for zero value. Keep an in-memory map in the API process, flush every 5 minutes in one batched UPDATE, and only write rows over a day stale; day precision is plenty for a 30-day rule.

nodes.label: Eviction Beats Compression, For Derivatives Only
nodes.rationale: Source blobs: compress hard, never delete, ref_count guards removal. Derivatives: never compress, evict freely, since kernel_version plus params_json make regeneration deterministic. The UI wording is a product rule — say render cache, show what it reclaims, and state that source files are untouched.

nodes.label: Thumbnails As bytea In Postgres
nodes.rationale: The deliberate exception to 'no blobs in Postgres': WebP under 64 KB inline on the derivative row so it arrives in the same query as the grid page instead of costing 100 filesystem round trips per scroll. Worth more to perceived speed than any compression decision, and the reason skipping the store upgrade does not break the grid.

nodes.label: Deletion Is Three Steps
nodes.rationale: Delete sets deleted_at and touches no disk; purge is a separate, explicitly worded action refused on a part not deleted first, and recomputes ref_count rather than decrementing because a counter maintained by increments drifts and the thing that acts on the drift deletes bytes; quarantine holds the bytes 30 days. Keep the three apart in every string — wording that lets one read as another is a defect.

nodes.label: Two Quarantines, One Timer
nodes.rationale: blob.quarantined_at is per hash and enters when a recomputed ref_count reaches zero; quarantined_file is per store-relative path and enters when the one part owning that file is purged. Source dedup is gone, so one hash can be several model files with independent lifetimes, which is why the path cannot live on the blob row. Migration 0014 gives both the same 30 days from one constant, because a second retention would be a second promise to explain in the same dialog.

nodes.label: Quarantine Is A Timestamp, Not A quarantine/ Tree
nodes.rationale: The bytes do not move, so restoring needs no path rewrite and no reader needs a second lookup location on the hot path to serve a rare case. What actually keeps a referenced blob safe is neither the counter nor the reaper's WHERE clause but file.blake3 and derivative.blake3 foreign keys; the reachability check merely lets the reaper decline a row rather than fail the whole sweep. Nothing references file.storage_path, so there the check is the only protection.

nodes.label: LOD Ladder — L0 At Ingest, L1 And L2 On Demand
nodes.rationale: Reverses the earlier 'all generated at ingest' rule on two new facts. Slice 3 measured L0 7.3 MB, L1 41 MB, L2 52 MB over 150 files — 93% of the bytes in rungs the grid never opens; slice 4 writes 7.5 MB, a 92.5% drop. And compose's ceilings say the stack targets a modest workstation, so spending 93 MB per 150 parts on rungs nothing asked for is spending somebody else's disk. L0 still builds at ingest, so the open path still has bytes to paint; if refine reads slow the answer is a background sweep, not three rungs per part.

nodes.label: meshopt, Not Draco
nodes.rationale: Draco compresses 15-20% smaller but meshopt decodes roughly an order of magnitude faster and is SIMD-friendly, and decode latency dominates for visual triage. Draco is encoded additionally only for the cloud tier where egress bytes cost money.

nodes.label: Immutable Blob Caching
nodes.rationale: /api/blob/{blake3} can never return different bytes, so max-age=31536000, immutable, an ETag of the hash and range support come free from content addressing — repeat opens hit the browser cache with no round trip and no invalidation logic. But every blob request must still verify the principal reaches a part referencing it.

nodes.label: Prefetch On Intent
nodes.rationale: Hover a card prefetches L0; opening the inspector prefetches L1 for the neighbours in sort order. Bound the pool at 2 and cancel on navigate, or fast scrolling saturates the queue with parts already passed.

nodes.label: Performance Targets As Regression Tests
nodes.rationale: Grid page of 100 under 80 ms warm, part open to first paint under 120 ms, open to L2 under 600 ms, search over 100k parts under 150 ms, facet counts under 300 ms. Treated as tests, not aspirations.

nodes.label: Five Extraction Stages, Each Committing Independently
nodes.rationale: Identity (always succeeds, and a known hash short-circuits everything), structural, geometric, semantic, derived. A stage-4 failure still leaves a usable, searchable part.

nodes.label: Columns vs JSONB — One Rule
nodes.rationale: If it appears in a filter, sort or facet it is a typed column with an index; everything else is JSONB. ORDER BY (metadata->>'volume')::float is unindexable in practice and becomes a seq scan at ~50k rows.

nodes.label: Core Schema
nodes.rationale: part / revision / file / blob / derivative / part_source / part_image, on uuid v7 with a STORED tsvector. Two deviations from the sketch are built and deliberate: position rather than is_primary on part_image, because a part carries an ordered gallery a boolean could not express, and bytes inline or in a blob at the same 64 KB line, so the store has one rule about small images rather than two.

nodes.label: Dual Index: tsvector Plus pg_trgm
nodes.rationale: to_tsvector('english','A1234-56-B') mangles identifiers, so searching 1234 will not find it — this bites every parts application eventually. Run both indexes, union, and rank trigram similarity above text rank when the query looks like an identifier. Turkish needs a language column on library, because the tsvector config is fixed at index time.

nodes.label: 10k Exact-Count Facet Threshold
nodes.rationale: Under 10k matching rows, exact counts in one query with FILTER aggregates; above that, a rollup or no counts at all. Users tolerate missing counts; they do not tolerate a 900 ms filter panel.

nodes.label: Custom Fields, Max 8 Indexed
nodes.rationale: Values live in part.metadata_json with a matching expression index when indexed. Capped at 8 because each is a write cost on every ingest.

nodes.label: Non-Destructive Image Framing
nodes.rationale: fit, focus_x and focus_y are CSS object-fit and object-position applied by the browser at display time, so the stored WebP is never re-encoded and adjusting the framing is free, reversible, and costs no generation of quality.

nodes.label: Do Not Build A Scraper
nodes.rationale: Three source-link paths in order — upload, paste an image URL (fetch once, store as a blob, never hotlink because hosts rotate URLs and hotlinking leaks a referrer on every grid scroll), and an explicit OpenGraph fetch button. Systematic harvesting breaks on every redesign and violates GrabCAD and TraceParts ToS specifically.

nodes.label: Fetching A User-Supplied URL Is SSRF
nodes.rationale: Resolve DNS first and check the resolved IP against RFC1918, loopback, link-local (169.254.169.254 especially), ULA and mapped-v4, re-checking after every redirect for DNS rebinding. http/https only, 3 redirects, 10 s, 10 MB enforced while streaming, content-type and magic bytes, explicit image::Limits because a 200 KB PNG can declare 50000x50000 and take the process out. Re-encoding to bounded WebP normalizes, mitigates bombs and strips EXIF GPS in one step.

nodes.label: Download variant=original, Re-Hashed Before Serving
nodes.rationale: original is the only legal value today; variant=3mf is a 400 naming what to send, never a silent fallback. The route re-hashes the bytes and refuses with 500 on mismatch, which is what makes 'verifiable against the stored BLAKE3' true rather than asserted, at microseconds against the transfer. Cache-Control: no-cache, because this URL names a revision whose source could be re-pointed, unlike the blob route whose URL contains the hash. RFC 5987 filenames, because Turkish part names contain g-breve, s-cedilla and dotless i.

nodes.label: Hash First, Client-Side, Then Probe
nodes.rationale: BLAKE3 in WASM before uploading, then POST /api/uploads/probe returns have/need so 480 of 500 dragged files never transfer. Resumable chunked upload is mandatory — a 2 GB STEP over a corporate VPN as one POST will fail at 90% — and the server verifies the assembled hash against the client's claim, because it is the dedup key and a wrong one silently corrupts another user's part.

nodes.label: Streaming ZIP Bundles, STORE Not DEFLATE
nodes.rationale: Never buffered server-side; contents are already compressed so deflating again burns CPU for nothing. manifest.json with part numbers, revisions, hashes and source licences makes the bundle verifiable rather than a folder of mystery files.

nodes.label: Archive Security
nodes.rationale: 3MF is a ZIP and therefore a zip-bomb vector: cap decompressed size, entry count and compression ratio during extraction and abort on breach, not after. Reject absolute paths and .. segments — old, still exploited.

nodes.label: Geometric Diff Replaces Textual Diff
nodes.rationale: Delta volume, bbox per axis, mass and centre of mass, triangle/face/edge counts, plus an overlay with the old as a grey ghost. Per-face Hausdorff is the premium version: expensive, async, cached, and never in the synchronous diff path.

nodes.label: External Round-Trip Watcher Rules
nodes.rationale: Checkout to a flat human-readable workspace folder because users open it in a file manager. Debounce 500 ms then wait for write-settle; ignore editor scratch files; hash before believing anything, since editors touch mtime constantly without changing content and identical bytes are not a revision. Windows ReadDirectoryChangesW overflows a fixed kernel buffer during bulk operations and silently drops events, so handle overflow with a full rescan; macOS FSEvents coalesces at directory granularity. inotify does not propagate through Docker Desktop bind mounts on macOS or Windows, which is why the watcher lives in the native agent binary.

nodes.label: Be Honest About Which Tools Round-Trip
nodes.rationale: Rhino, FreeCAD, Blender, SolidWorks and the slicers write back the file we handed them; Fusion 360 and Onshape cannot, being cloud-backed. For those the honest flow is export-and-reimport and the UI must say so — overpromising destroys trust in version history, which is the feature everything else hangs on.

hyperedges.label: Delete, Purge, Quarantine And Cache Eviction Kept Apart
